runs.text: Lalit R. Mishra is the author of The Human Fiction series.
He is not writing from a position of authority, but from observation — of thought, identity, and the subtle narratives through which human experience organizes itself.
His work explores a simple but uncomfortable question:
what if the “self” is not something we find, but something that is continuously constructed?
Rather than presenting fixed answers, his writing focuses on examining the hidden structures behind everyday experience — memory, language, interpretation, inner narration, and the sense of becoming.
He is particularly interested in how a stable “I” appears to exist, even though it is never found as a single, fixed entity in direct experience.
His approach is not philosophical declaration, but careful observation.
Not conclusion, but clarity emerging through attention.
The Human Fiction reflects this perspective — exploring how identity, meaning, and personal continuity are formed through narrative patterns that operate silently in the background of awareness.
In his view, most of what we call “self” is not discovered…
And most of what we call “life” is not directly interpreted…
This work is not meant to be taken as truth or rejected as fiction.
It is meant to be seen as structure.
no longer holds the same unconscious authority it once did.
